newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Seized Britons say Colombia drug cargo is "mix-up".
newsitem.headline: Seized Britons say Colombia drug cargo is "mix-up".

text.p: Three Britons being held on charges of trying to smuggle $50 million of cocaine out of Colombia aboard a luxury yacht said on Sunday their arrest was a "mix-up" and that they hoped to be released soon.

Michael Hayne, 50, from Egham, his son Stephen Alan, 27, of Ashford, and David Maurice Shaw, 49, of Oldham, were arrested by the state security service DAS in the Caribbean coast port of Barranquilla on Friday evening.

More than 425 pounds (194 kg) of high purity cocaine, with an estimated value of $50 million, was found in the U.S.-registered yacht Perla del Mar in which the trio were travelling, a DAS spokesman alleged.

"This whole thing is a huge mix-up. Everything will be straightened out very soon. The conditions in the jail are fine and we're being treated OK," ship's captain Michael Hayne told Reuters in a phone interview from Barranquilla's El Bosque jail, where the trio are in custody.

The men are due to be questioned by prosecutors on Monday, the DAS spokesman said. If they are found guilty of drug trafficking they face between four and 12 years behind bars. Those terms could, however, be slashed by at least one-third in return for a full admission of guilt and for providing details of illicit narcotics suppliers to Colombian judges.
The DAS spokesman said it was believed the men purchased the vessel in the nearby port city of Cartagena a week ago and that it was bound for Martinique or the Virgin Islands.
A British embassy spokesman in Bogota was unable to give details about the three men, saying that he was awaiting information from Barranquilla.

The DAS said Shaw's passport had been issued by the British High Commissioner in Trinidad, while Michael Hayne had obtained his from the British Consulate in Madrid. All three have been communicating with the authorities through an interpreter.
